tossups.question: In this decade, a journalist exposed the Copper Green program. John Yoo authored a controversial series of memos during this decade. tossups.question: The Ricardian equivalence proposition argues these things have the same effect as government bonds. tossups.question: To prevent the multiple comparisons problem from increasing the number of these events, scientists may utilize the Bonferroni correction. There is an inverse trade-off between decreasing the probability of one of these events and the power of a test. Statistical hypothesis tests represent the probability of these events as alpha, or the significance level. Type 1 errors are an alternative name for these events that result from incorrectly rejecting the null hypothesis. For 10 points, misdiagnosing a healthy patient is an example of what type of statistical error contrasted with false negatives?
tossups.answer: false positives [accept false alarms; accept type 1 errors until read; prompt on errors until read]

tossups.question: The August Decrees ended a feudal system in response to a period of “Great Fear” spurred on by an attack on this location. A group carrying more than 30,000 muskets marched on this location after being unable to get gunpowder from the Hôtel des Invalides (“oh-TELL days on-vah-LEED”). tossups.question: A 2020 University of Notre Dame staging of one musical starred Teagan Earley as this character, who calls his teacher a “sad, pathetic man” before comparing him to a “jaded mandarin.” According to Robert de Boron, the Arthurian Siege Perilous was inspired by the seat this character vacated during a feast. tossups.question: Bertram Lupov and Alexander Adell pose the title inquiry of a story by this author that ends by stating “LET THERE BE LIGHT.” This author described the impact of seeing stars on the darkness-averse population of Lagash in the short story “Nightfall.” In a novel by this author, Hari Seldon’s field of psychohistory foretells the fall of the Galactic Empire. tossups.question: A member of this phylum has over 12 types of photoreceptors, allowing it to detect the circular polarization of light. Segmented bodies, jointed appendages, and chitinous exoskeletons characterize members of this phylum. For 10 points, name this phylum whose members include arachnids, crustaceans, and insects.

tossups.question: A character in this novel imagines Lucie naming her child after him after sharing a kiss with a seamstress and saying, “I am the resurrection and the life.” In the first section of this novel, a man employed at Tellson’s bank receives a message that reads “Recalled to life.” In this novel, men all referred to as “Jacques” gather at the wine shop of Madame Defarge, who constantly knits the names of people to be killed. Lucretius’ De Rerum Natura (“day RAY-room nah-TOO-rah”) presents a “symmetry argument” about this concept that expands upon Epicurus’s observation that this concept has “no subject of harm” since it causes no pain beyond expectations of it. tossups.question: In a work set during this event, the narrator teaches Italian to Jean by reciting Ulysses’s speech from Dante’s Inferno. tossups.question: Note to moderator: read the answerline carefully. Lucius Minucius Augurinus (“LOO-kee-us min-OO-kee-us ow-gur-EE-nus”) was the first prefect appointed to oversee this good, inspected via sealed sample-jars to prevent adulteration. The cura annonae (“KOO-rah ah-NO-nye”) was the main system of procuring and distributing this good, whose price was set by Gaius Gracchus and later changed to five modii (“MO-dee-ee”). Clodius Pulcher massively expanded this good’s “dole,” a social welfare system to which olive oil, wine, and pork were later added. parts: What ancient rock-cut “rose city” is located in modern-day Jordan?
Rome formed the province of Arabia Petraea after the death of a king with this epithet, Rabbel II. Ptolemy I also had this epithet which means “savior.”
Arabia Petraea was later taken from the Byzantines by this empire in what has sometimes been called the Last Great War of Antiquity. This Persian empire was ruled by Ardashir I and Shapur I.
answers: Sassanid Empire [or Sasanian Empire or Eranshahr; reject “Safavid Empire” and “Saffarid Dynasty” and “Samanid Dynasty”]
